analysis.session_summary: The window was driven by broad USD weakness and CHF outperformance, with risk-off signals from a rising VIX. AUD was the weakest currency after a sharp employment miss (-39.3K vs 19.6K), while GBP gained on a GDP beat (0.1% vs -0.1%). Strong US retail sales (0.8% vs 0.3%) failed to lift the dollar, leaving many legs without clear catalysts.

themes.evidence: CHF +0.754% strongest, closed at its best; USD/CHF -98.8 pips, -1.179%; VIX +2.572%.
AUD -1.163% weakest; Employment Change -39.3K vs 19.6K, AUD/USD -50.6 pips.
GDP m/m 0.1% vs -0.1%; GBP +0.372%; GBP/USD +106.5 pips.
Retail Sales 0.8% vs 0.3% but USD basket -0.038%, inside noise floor; DXY -0.684%.

currency_drivers.USD: No clear catalyst; strong retail sales beat failed to lift the dollar.
currency_drivers.EUR: No euro-specific releases; moved mainly on cross flows and USD weakness.
currency_drivers.JPY: No Japanese releases; early strength attempt rejected and gave back 92%.
currency_drivers.GBP: GDP beat at 0.1% vs -0.1% supported GBP; Bailey speech was muted.
currency_drivers.AUD: Employment miss (-39.3K vs 19.6K) drove AUD sharply weaker.
currency_drivers.CAD: No Canada releases; selling to -0.19% was rejected, recovering 82%.
currency_drivers.CHF: No clear catalyst; SNB Schlegel was muted, yet CHF closed at its best.
currency_drivers.NZD: No New Zealand releases; modest strength while AUD sank.

leg_notes.EUR/USD: EUR/USD's initial 107.3-pip rally lacked a clear catalyst and then faded only 28.2 pips into the close, leaving the pair up 83.5 pips with USD weakness the main driver.

polarity_reads.read: Normal reaction: miss surprise weakened AUD 0.258%; market was positioned for upside and aggressively sold AUD crosses.
Muted reaction: despite 0.8% vs 0.3% beat, USD basket moved only -0.038%, inside noise floor; suggests USD not being bought on strong US data.
Muted reaction: basket -0.019%, no directional impulse; CHF strength not driven by speaker.
Normal reaction: beat surprise strengthened GBP 0.041%; GBP demand already present, amplified by data.
Muted reaction: basket -0.007%, no information; did not alter GBP tone.

scenarios.name: Soft USD / CHF strength extends
scenarios.thesis: Broad USD weakness persists despite strong US data, and CHF safe-haven demand remains supported by elevated VIX.
triggers: US yields fail to rise on strong data
No hawkish surprise from Fed Chairman Warsh
scenarios.invalidation: US yields jump sharply or risk sentiment stabilizes strongly

pair_paths.rationale: USD weakness dominated today with EUR/USD range at 118.7 pips; no EUR catalyst to stop it.
CHF closed at its best and USD/CHF fell 98.8 pips; extension targets its 113.9 daily range.
AUD remains weakest after employment miss; daily range 86.2 pips supports further downside.

scenarios.name: USD recovery on data repricing
scenarios.thesis: Market belatedly rewards strong US retail sales and PPI; USD squeezes higher against recent losers, especially JPY and EUR.
scenarios.invalidation: USD remains unresponsive to positive US data or DXY breaks below 101.882

pair_paths.rationale: USD/JPY range was 123.5 pips; recovery likely toward upper end if yen loses safe-haven bid.
EUR/USD daily range 118.7 pips; USD recovery can retrace the 83.5 pip gain.

scenarios.name: Cross-currents and consolidation
scenarios.thesis: No dominant catalyst; pairs hold recent ranges as markets await fresh cues from central bank speakers.
scenarios.invalidation: A decisive break in EUR/USD or USD/CHF outside today's ranges

pair_paths.rationale: Pair likely stays within today's 118.7-pip range absent new catalyst.
USD/CHF may consolidate within its 113.9 daily range as CHF strength pauses.

risks.risk: Strong US data is not lifting USD
risks.why_it_matters: If market ignores 0.8% retail sales, USD downside may be larger than positioning suggests.
Risk-off flows are favoring CHF over USD; could accelerate in thin liquidity.
AUD -1.163% and employment miss may lead to further unwinding.

analysis.calendar_ahead_note: Coming window has central bank speakers only: BOE's Bailey at 04:00, Fed Chairman Warsh at 05:30, and BOC's Macklem at 06:15. Warsh is the main USD risk; any hawkish shift could reverse the muted USD response.
